title: Predicting preterm birth using machine learning techniques in oral microbiome.
summary: In 59 singleton pregnancies, random-forest analysis of oral microbiome data reported 25 differentially abundant taxa and a nine-taxon classifier with balanced accuracy 0.765 ± 0.071 under five-fold cross-validation. A separate nine-pregnancy twin sample had reported accuracy of 87.5%; both samples are small and do not establish clinical utility.
ai_technology: A random-forest classifier used oral microbiome composition to predict preterm birth and rank informative taxa; differential-abundance analysis separately identified candidate taxa.
organization: Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, University of Ulsan College of Medicine, Asan Medical Center, Seoul, Republic of Korea; Department of Biomedical Engineering, Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology, Republic of Korea; Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Jeonbuk National University Medical School, Republic of Korea; Research Institute of Clinical Medicine, Jeonbuk National University Hospital, Republic of Korea; Helixco Inc., Republic of Korea; Department of Pharmacology, Jeonbuk National University Medical School, Republic of Korea

evidence.tested: The singleton cohort yielded 25 differentially abundant taxa; a nine-taxon classifier reported balanced accuracy 0.765 ± 0.071, while the separate twin sample had reported accuracy 87.5%.
evidence.unknown: Stratified five-fold cross-validation in 59 singleton pregnancies and a separate nine-twin sample. The cohorts are small and from the study setting; prospective utility and multicenter validation are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning analysis identified oral microbiome taxa associated with preterm birth and reported predictive performance in small pregnancy cohorts.

source_review.scope: Primary Scientific Reports full text, including cohort, model evaluation and Results; publication date checked against the publisher record.
